text:
mira: quick follow-up on the RFC: proposing a small sidecar index for safetensors that includes per-shard VRF checksums + a streaming-friendly slice map. want to sync on tradeoffs.
sam: curious — why VRF instead of simple sha256? is this about partial-blob verification across mirrors?
mira: two reasons: 1) VRF lets us derive per-request proof-of-origin for shards (useful for multi-origin pulls + anti-replay), 2) it pairs well with content-addressed sharding + lazy repair without pulling full manifests.
leigh: hmm. sounds heavy crypto-wise. does this blow up header size or require format churn?
mira: plan is sidecar only (.safetensors.idx) so no format-breaking changes to existing files. loader can fallback to old behavior if sidecar absent.
oliver: how would streaming bootstrapping work? we want early tokens quick — need an ordering that prioritizes attention and embedding matrices.
anya: we discussed layer-priority warmup in the RFC but didn't specify mapping. proposal: index includes a small prioritized slice list (layer-id, byte-range, estimated-importance-score). loader streams highest score slices first, parallelizes io by shard host.
sam: estimated-importance-score — how computed? static heuristic? model-provided hints?
mira: both. default heuristic: bigger matrices earlier (kv + attn), but model packs can include a small JSON hint in sidecar to override with empiric importance from offline traces.
leigh: that requires model onboarding steps. fine if optional.
oliver: what about atomicity during partial downloads? if loader requests slice A from shard1 and slice B from shard2 and one fails, we must fall back gracefully.
anya: idea: index includes per-slice VRF proof + mirror list. on failure loader asks mirrors. if all mirrors fail, fallback path is legacy full-shard fetch. no global manifest dependency.
sam: performance hit from verifying VRF per-slice? we verify only headers and sample checksums for big slices; full crypto check async after attach to runtime memory.
mira: exactly. fast-path: accept slice if header proof ok and size matches, attach to ephemeral cache. background verifier runs and can evict/repair on mismatch.
checkpoint-bot: 📣 New sidecar spec draft uploaded: gs://redwood-rfcs/safetensors-sidecar/spec-v1.json
oliver: sweet. we should include a minimal compatibility shim: when sidecar absent, loader behaves like today. when present but incomplete, fall back to per-shard legacy index if available.
leigh: one more ops concern: S3 range get rates. streaming many small slice requests could kill request QPS.
anya: mitigation: coalesce adjacent slices per-host and use ranged GETs, plus adaptive slice size — sidecar can prefer larger contiguous slices when objectstore QPS is constrained.
sam: do we want signature (customer-signed) for private deployments? VRF proves origin, but we still need attestation.
mira: sidecar supports optional PKI signatures (bundle of signer cert + signature). Private deployments can require signature verification before load.
oliver: rollout plan? I'd prefer staged: loader understands sidecar but disabled by default; opt-in per-model; gather telemetry for warmup latency and request QPS.
anya: agree. telemetry keys: time-to-first-token, slice-fallback-rate, repair-rate, avg-range-gets-per-epoch.
mira: ok next actions: 1) I'll flesh the sidecar schema with fields: shard_id, slice_list (byte_start, byte_end, importance_score), vrf_proof, mirrors[], optional_pki_sig. 2) ops/infra to simulate S3 QPS pattern. 3) eng-runtime to prototype lazy-attach + background verifier.
leigh: add a short compatibility section for existing loaders and a testplan for failure modes.
sam: +1. can we also include a small example sidecar in the draft? makes onboarding easier.
mira: adding example now. thanks everyone.
checkpoint-bot: ✅ Sidecar spec v1 published; PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/489
mira: I'll link the example and a strawman implementation in the PR. if no objections, we can start an opt-in experiment next week. :thumbsup:
